title: incident-bot: improve on-call diagnostics ranking and SLO runbook linking
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: on-call responders rely on high-quality, prioritized runbook suggestions when the incident-bot surfaces automated diagnostics. We observed several incidents where the suggested runbooks were low-relevance or omitted critical SLO-linked runbooks. This PR improves runbook ranking heuristics, tightens SLO -> runbook linking, and adds on-call helper context to increase signal-to-noise for responders.

Changes: - Implement a lightweight runbook scoring pipeline that considers SLO similarity, recent successful runbook hits, owner proximity (same team), and a recency decay factor. - Add SLO tagging improvements to the slo-toolkit utilities to surface stronger links (matching by service, metric, and alert fingerprint). - Integrate ranking into the incident-bot suggestions flow and expose top-N reasons in the suggestion payload. - Add telemetry counters and histograms for ranking decisions and suggestion acceptance. - Add unit and integration tests for ranking, plus a small e2e smoke test that exercises runbook linking end-to-end.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc + Linear ticket referenced (ENG-4213)
- [x] Unit tests for ranking heuristics
- [x] Integration test for SLO -> runbook linking
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated
- [x] Backwards-compatible (no breaking changes)
- [x] Documentation update (README + console guidance)

Notes: Some changes touch a small API surface (suggestion payload) but maintain a compatibility layer. This landed as a squash merge after addressing review feedback. See linked Linear ticket for scoring weight rationale and experiments.
